title: Chunked repair manifest protocol for resumable structured-tool outputs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Tool/function calling with streaming structured JSON output can be interrupted mid-object due to network truncation, client disconnects, or server-side preemption. Existing resume/retry guidance is ad-hoc and leads to incorrect tool-call state, duplicated side effects, and brittle client logic.

Goal: Define a practical, backwards-compatible protocol and SDK guidance to make streaming structured outputs (JSON/NDJSON) resumable and repairable for tool calls while preserving idempotency signals and minimizing coupling between client and runtime. Provide a server-side manifest to allow robust reassembly, quick validation, and safe retries without requiring full change to existing streaming endpoints.

Scope: streaming JSON and NDJSON produced by model->tool and model->client flows, tool-call boundary preservation, escape/UTF8 truncation heuristics, per-chunk checksums, resume tokens, and an optional post-stream manifest that enables server-assisted repair and fast resume. Not in scope: changes to tool-side business logic to enforce idempotency (we will provide guidance but not enforce).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Protocol defined and documented in RFC for engineers and SDKs. 2) Runtime emits per-chunk metadata (fragment_id, seq, crc32c, byte_range) and an end-of-stream manifest when available. 3) SDKs (python/js) can resume a stream using resume_token and reconstruct the original JSON even when truncated mid-codepoint. 4) No regression on non-tool streaming endpoints. 5) E2E tests for common truncation cases (UTF8 split, escape sequence partials, nested-object truncation) pass in CI.
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Chunk envelope: every stream chunk MAY be preceded with an ASCII envelope line that is an L-JSON metadata record (len prefixed) to avoid breaking existing consumers. Example envelope keys: fragment_id, seq, crc32c, final_flag (true when chunk contains end-of-object), resume_hint. 2) Tombstone marker: when stream truncation is detected server-side we emit a lightweight tombstone envelope that marks a safe cutpoint and includes a short repair_hint (base64 sampled suffix) so clients can attempt client-side stitch before contacting server. 3) Manifest: optional end-of-stream manifest emitted as a final envelope (manifest=true) containing the canonical sequence, byte offsets, and a per-segment hash list. This enables shorter reconstructions and lightweight verification. 4) Resume token: servers issue opaque resume_token header/field after authentication that encodes model-instance, request-id, last-seq, and expiry. Clients supply resume_token and next_seq to request a resume; server either sends missing chunks or a delta manifest. 5) Escape repair heuristics: SDKs should try a two-pass repair: UTF8 byte re-alignment then JSON token reconciliation via a small deterministic suffix/prefix heuristic. If repair fails, fall back to requesting server-side replay using resume_token. 6) Backwards compatibility: streams without envelopes continue to work but lose resume capabilities; SDKs detect absence and fall back to current behavior.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement chunk envelope generator in runtime, crc32c computation, resume_token issuance, and manifest emission flag. Add feature flag and opt-in header X-RW-Stream-Manifest. Phase 2 (1 sprint): python/js SDK changes to parse envelopes, perform repair heuristics, and resume flows. Phase 3 (1 sprint): add e2e tests, chaos truncation harness, and integration with tool-call idempotency advisories. Phase 4 (rollout): staged behind feature flag, enable for select heavy customers, collect metrics, then full release.

Server endpoints touched: /v1/streams (streaming output path), tool-call coordinator. Low-risk toggles will be behind runtime gate.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope encoder/decoder, crc verification, resume token parsing. Integration tests for: 1) UTF8-split truncation: ensure SDK can repair 3-byte UTF8 sequence split across chunks. 2) Escape sequence truncation: ensure backslash escapes are not left dangling. 3) Nested-object mid-field truncation: SDK requests server replay and merges. 4) Simulated packet loss: randomized chunk drop and resume. Add fuzz harness in CI that mutates chunk boundaries. Add telemetry assertions to make sure repair occurs <2% for healthy runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind X-RW-Stream-Manifest and org-level opt-in. 2) Enable in canary cluster for internal Redwood CLI customers. 3) Monitor: stream-resume-success, avg-repair-latency, duplicate-tool-invokes (critical). 4) Disable gate if duplicate-tool-invokes > 0.01% over 10k calls. 5) After 2 weeks stable, enable for more customers, then default-on in runtime-1.22.
dependencies_notes: Depends on existing stream framing improvements (ENG-41209) for envelope compatibility and the structured-output fallback work in ENG-21456. Customer-facing rollout will require console feature flag UI changes (Product).
security_considerations: Resume tokens are opaque and time-limited; do not leak resume tokens in client logs. Manifest may contain small samples of payload; ensure PII is redacted according to existing PII policy. Note to infra: rotate resume token HMAC keys during key rotation windows carefully to avoid invalidating active resumes.
migration_notes: Existing SDKs will continue to work with older servers. New SDKs will gracefully detect envelope presence by probing first line. Migration docs and sample code will be added to the quickstart. Recommend contacting top 10 customers with heavy streaming usage to opt into beta.
open_questions: What is the max size of manifest we are willing to emit (customers with huge outputs)?
Should resume_token be single-use or multi-resume for short window?
Do we require tool authors to return idempotency keys for side-effecting tools or rely on advisory docs?
